title: Memory-aware KV shard coordination across tensor+pipeline parallelism
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Problem statement:
We are running out of usable GPU DRAM for large-context models when combining tensor parallel (TP) and pipeline parallel (PP) for high-throughput inference. Replicating the KV cache across TP replicas or naively sharding it by whole layers leads to either excessive memory overhead or runtime stalls during cross-device KV gather/scatter. This ticket designs and implements a memory-aware KV sharding scheme that cooperates with our TP+PP layouts and the continuous-batching runtime to reduce peak memory usage while keeping tail latency within SLOs.

Goals:
- Reduce peak per-GPU KV memory by at least 30% for 64k-context workloads on 8x A100-class clusters without increasing median latency by more than 5% and tail P95 by more than 15%.
- Provide compatibility with dynamic continuous batching: requests can arrive at arbitrary sequence lengths and micro-batch composition must not trigger expensive global synchronization.
- Keep implementation incremental: fallback to current replicated KV behavior behind a feature flag and provide a clear rollout/monitoring plan.

Design overview (high level):
1) Hybrid fine-grained KV tiling: split KV tensors along sequence and head dimension into small tiles (~64-256 tokens worth per tile depending on model), then place tiles across devices according to a placement policy that balances memory and reduces cross-device access. Tiles are the unit of movement for gather/scatter.
2) Placement policy aware of TP/PP mapping: the scheduler reads model-parallel topology (tensor shards and pipeline stages) and prioritizes placing tiles on devices that will next consume them (locality-first). For KV that will be consumed by later pipeline stages, we bias placement toward downstream stages to minimize early-stage scatter.
3) Lazy remote splice + async prefetch: introduce a non-blocking prefetch RPC that fetches remote tiles ahead of micro-batch execution using continuous-batching horizon estimates. If prefetch misses, we perform an on-the-fly splice with lightweight coordinator to avoid global barrier.
4) Memory compaction and eviction: implement LRU-like eviction of oldest prefix tiles, with adaptive thresholding based on free-memory signals from the CUDA allocator. Evicted tiles are checkpointed to local NVMe if configured for Private deployments.
5) Quantization and alignment compatibility: tile format is quantization-friendly (supports 4-bit/8-bit compressed storage) and keeps alignment compatible with optimized kernels to avoid dequantization overheads in hot paths.

Implementation tasks (planned order):
- Instrument current KV layout to emit per-tensor/per-shard lifetime and access heatmaps (profiling PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/PR-xxxx).
- Implement tile allocator and placement policy module inside runtime allocator layer (new module: kv_tile_allocator).
- Add non-blocking prefetch API to the request scheduler and make continuous-batcher expose lookahead estimates for prefetch triggers.
- Implement async remote splice path using NCCL P2P and a lightweight rendezvous to avoid global allreduce for small transfers.
- Add eviction + NVMe spill fallback for Private deployments behind flags.
- Integrate with rollout flags and metrics (kv_tile_evictions, kv_remote_prefetch_hits, kv_remote_splice_latency, per-gpu-kv-mem).

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests cover tile allocation, placement, prefetch hit/miss behavior, and eviction correctness.
- End-to-end perf test shows >=30% KV mem reduction on the target configuration with median latency increase <=5% and P95 <=15% of baseline.
- Feature flag exists and default behavior remains current replicated KV until ramped.
- PR includes a migration note and a console dashboard tile for the new KV metrics.

Rollout and monitoring plan:
- Stage 0: internal nightly cluster runs for functional verification (1 week).
- Stage 1: shadow mode for a small percentage of hosted traffic (5%) to validate perf and prefetch hit ratios.
- Stage 2: opt-in beta for Dedicated customers with clear mem savings reporting.
- Stage 3: global rollout if no regressions.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Complexity: fine-grained tiling and placement increases scheduler complexity and code paths for KV access. Mitigation: small tile size and incremental feature-flagged rollout, extensive unit tests.
- Synchronization overhead: prefetch mitigates blocking gathers but adds network bandwidth and potential head-of-line effect. Mitigation: adaptive prefetch thresholds and locality-first placement to minimize cross-device transfers.
- Debuggability: remote splices and evictions complicate reproducing failures. Mitigation: deterministic tracing mode that records tile placements and fetch events for a request id.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Synthetic replay harness derived from internal request traces to simulate mix of short/long contexts and continuous-batcher micro-batch patterns (link: https://go.redwood/internal/kv-tiling-harness).
- Perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood/runtime/kv-tiling/ (will be created by ENG infra).

Artifacts and references:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Memory-aware+KV+Sharding
- Prototype PR with allocator changes: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/PR-xxxx
- Related tickets: ENG-7420 (multi-gpu KV shard strategy), ENG-8602 (kv shard protocol), ENG-9231 (kv slab sharding hybrid-parallel).

Open questions:
- Optimal tile size heuristics across different model families and batch mixes (experimentation required).
- NVMe checkpoint format and eviction latency bounds for air-gapped on-prem deployments.
- Interaction with future model caching features (prefix reuse across requests) and whether tile deduplication is useful.
